business_scope.primary_industry_name: Automated Subtitle Transcription and AI Voice Cloning Studio

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (written legal system rooted in the Napoleonic Code; unitary national jurisdiction without separate sub-state company-law regimes, except for certain overseas collectivities excluded from this filing)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) - Freedom of Establishment (Article 49) and Free Movement of Capital (Article 63)
France-China Agreement on the Reciprocal Encouragement and Protection of Investments (signed 28 May 2007, in force since 6 November 2010)
France-China Double Taxation Agreement (signed 26 November 2013, applicable from 1 January 2015)
France-United States Convention for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (signed 31 August 1994, as amended by the 2006 and 2009 Protocols)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Articles L.561-1 to L.561-50 and R.561-1 et seq. of the Code monétaire et financier (CMF), in particular Article L.561-2-2 (beneficial-owner definition; 25% ownership/control threshold), Articles L.561-45 to L.561-49 (UBO declaration and register, penalty provision at L.561-49: up to six months' imprisonment and EUR 7,500 fine, multiplied by five for legal persons under Article 131-38 of the Code pénal), Article L.561-10 (customer due diligence) and Article L.561-15 (declaration de soupçon to Tracfin); Law No. 2016-1691 of 9 December 2016 (Sapin II); Law No. 2018-898 of 23 October 2018 (PACTE); Commercial Code Articles L.123-1, L.123-37, R.123-1 and R.123-28; Directive (EU) 2015/849 as amended by Directive (EU) 2018/843 (transposed); FATF Recommendations 10, 24 and 25.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access - restricted access with legitimate-interest disclosure; general public access was annulled by Conseil d'État Decision No. 434136 of 8 October 2020; inspection rights are limited to French authorities, AML/CFT obliged entities conducting due diligence, and persons demonstrating a legitimate interest.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foreign corporate registration excerpt or certificate of good standing of any corporate shareholder (Kbis equivalent)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry in the shareholder's state of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille plus sworn French translation; consular legalization required if the issuing state is not a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national identity card of each proposed shareholder, manager (gérant) and each signatory of the articles of association
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national civil registry or passport authority of the holder's country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified copy attested by a French sworn translator; apostille not required where originals are verifiable; consular attestation required for documents issued in non-Hague Convention states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Recent proof of residential address of each individual shareholder and manager (utility bill or official attestation issued within the preceding 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility supplier, municipality or public service authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Sworn translation into French; apostille not applicable to consumption invoices

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn translation into French of all foreign-language documents (traduction assermentée)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Sworn translator registered with a French Cour d'appel (Court of Appeal) or Tribunal judiciaire
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: No additional authentication required; the sworn translator's certification is the recognized authentication step for French public registries

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 governing sociétés à responsabilité limitée; Articles R.123-1 et seq. governing registration and company formalities; Article L.561-46 governing beneficial-owner declarations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: INPI Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises, with registration in the Registre national des entreprises (RNE); the competent commercial court registry performs the applicable commercial-register verification.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Electronic company-formation filing submitted through the Guichet unique, accompanied by the signed articles of association, beneficial-owner declaration, and supporting evidence for the registered office, management, capital deposit, and publication notice.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital is prescribed for a SARL; EUR 1 is legally sufficient. At least 20% of cash contributions must be paid upon incorporation, with the balance payable within five years of registration. Cash contributions are deposited into an account opened in the company's name, and the depositary issues a certificate of deposit. Contributions in kind must be fully transferred at incorporation. Official publication, beneficial-owner filing, depositary, professional, and bank charges are separate from the state formation filing fee.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST MANAGEMENT RESOLUTION OF THE SARL. The manager resolves that the company accepts the subscription by the founding shareholder(s) for the shares specified in the signed articles of association and acknowledges the deposit certificate for the paid-up cash contributions. The registered office is adopted at [full French address] with effect from registration. [Name] is appointed gérant for the statutory term, with authority to represent the company within the limits of French law and the articles. The manager is authorized to complete all filings with the INPI Guichet unique, the RNE, the commercial court registry, tax authorities, banks, and other competent authorities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm Corporate Identity, Activities, and Registered Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Select SARL formation, identify all shareholders and the gérant, state the principal activity as automated subtitle transcription, post-production, audio dubbing, and AI voice-cloning services, and provide the exact French registered-office address. Obtain written domiciliation or premises-use evidence before submission.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and principal activity
Signed domiciliation agreement, lease, or proof of premises ownership
Identification documents for shareholders and gérant
Foreign shareholder or manager residence and authority documents, where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct the electronic form and upload the requested evidence within the INPI query deadline; preserve the filing reference and submit a written explanation where the authority requests clarification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute Articles and Arrange Capital Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Chosen French credit institution, notary, or authorized depositary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Sign the articles of association, stating share capital, share allocation, management powers, registered office, accounting year, and transfer restrictions. Deposit at least 20% of cash contributions into an account opened for the company being formed. Obtain the formal certificate of deposit and retain evidence of the source of funds.
required_dossiers: Identity and address evidence for subscribers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Resolve bank compliance queries, correct shareholder or source-of-funds information, and obtain a replacement deposit certificate if the initial certificate contains an error.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized legal-announcement journal in the registered-office department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a formation notice containing the mandatory corporate particulars, including name, form, capital, registered office, purpose, duration, gérant identity, and registration location. Obtain the publication certificate or journal issue and upload it with the formation filing.
required_dossiers: Signed articles or corporate particulars used for the notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request correction or republication if a mandatory particular is inaccurate, then upload the corrected certificate and explain the correction in the INPI file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique, transmitting the file to the RNE and competent commercial court registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the electronic incorporation form, attach the signed articles, publication certificate, capital deposit certificate, registered-office evidence, manager declaration, identity documents, and beneficial-owner declaration. Sign electronically, pay any applicable registry or beneficial-owner charges shown by the portal, and monitor the filing reference.
required_dossiers: Translation or legalization documents where required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Answer registry requests through the portal, replace defective documents, correct inconsistent names or addresses, and resubmit before the stated deadline. A refusal may be challenged or resubmitted after curing the stated defect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receive Registration Evidence and Activate Operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique, RNE, commercial court registry, tax administration, and social-security interfaces
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Download the registration extract and verify the SIREN, SIRET, APE code, registered office, gérant, and activity description. Activate the permanent bank account, release deposited capital as permitted, arrange accounting records, register as an employer if staff are hired, and implement data-protection, copyright, employment, and AI-use controls.
required_dossiers: Registration extract or RNE registration evidence
Employment and payroll registration records, if applicable
Copyright, performer-consent, and voice-cloning authorization records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request correction of inaccurate registration data through the Guichet unique or competent registry and maintain evidence of the submitted correction until the public records are updated.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No general industrial licensing board is required for a French SARL conducting software-enabled subtitle transcription, audio post-production, dubbing, and AI voice-cloning services. Site-specific matters are handled, where applicable, by the relevant mairie, Préfecture, DREAL, occupational-health authorities, and fire-safety services.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No general manufacturing or operating permit applies to the described studio and post-production activity. A separate authorization may be required if the premises, equipment, emissions, storage, public access, or ancillary activity falls within a regulated regime, including the ICPE regime.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement (DREAL), under the competent regional Préfecture
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Ordinarily exempt from a project-level environmental impact assessment for ordinary office and audio post-production premises, subject to site-specific screening. An examination may arise for major construction, material alteration, regulated installations, significant energy use, waste treatment, or other projects listed under French environmental assessment rules.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No special wastewater or VOC threshold normally applies to a digital audio studio without industrial process discharges. Discharge wastewater only through an authorized network and comply with local sewer rules. Control solvents, cleaning products, and VOC-emitting equipment where used. Classify, store, document, and transfer hazardous and non-hazardous waste through authorized channels; retain waste tracking records where legally required. ICPE thresholds and permit conditions apply if regulated storage, combustion, waste, or emissions activities are introduced.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain landlord and municipal confirmation that the premises may be used for the declared activity. If the premises are open to the public, comply with établissement recevant du public rules, including fire-safety inspection, evacuation routes, emergency lighting, alarms, accessibility, and periodic control obligations. Maintain electrical, fire-extinguisher, ventilation, and structural-load inspection records. Conduct occupational-risk assessment, issue required workplace instructions, manage acoustic exposure and workstation risks, and complete mandatory employer declarations and occupational-health arrangements when personnel are employed.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) under the French Ministry of Economy and Finance; primary online portal impots.gouv.fr; company formation and registration portal formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities forming a French SARL must register through the formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr online single form with constitutive act, proof of registered office, director identity, and non-resident consent; upon approval the company obtains SIREN and SIRET numbers; DGFiP then attributes the French VAT number (FR + key + SIREN) once taxable activity commences; non-established foreign entities may need to appoint a tax representative in France and request a direct VAT registration from the competent Service des Impôts des Entreprises; all subsequent filings are made through impots.gouv.fr professional space
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France does not operate a check-the-box classification; a SARL is by default subject to French corporation tax (impôt sur les sociétés). Elective regimes include: (i) option for individual shareholders of eligible SARLs to be taxed at the shareholder level as a transparent entity under Article 239 bis A CGI for a maximum of five years; (ii) group tax integration (intégration fiscale) under Article 223 A CGI; (iii) option for the French VAT group (assujetti unique) regime; (iv) ATAD-aligned hybrid mismatch declarations under Article 212 bis CGI; (v) further constitutional election only through the DGIPF advance ruling procedure

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 85,000 for goods and EUR 37,500 for services for French-established entities; reduced thresholds EUR 42,500 for goods and EUR 18,750 for services for certain services and businesses when anti-abuse conditions apply; non-established foreign entities have no registration threshold and must register as soon as they make taxable supplies in France; intra-EU distance sales threshold EUR 10,000 for existing French VAT and OSS use
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France mandates the transition to mandatory e-invoicing and e-reporting through the Portail Public de Facturation (PPF) integrated with accredited Dematerialization Platforms (PDPs). The rollout is phased: large and mid-size companies from September 2026, small and medium-sized undertakings from September 2027. All e-invoices must be transmitted in an EN 16931-compliant structured format (Factur-X, UBL, CII), processed in near real-time, authenticated with a qualified digital signature or secure imprint, and cleared through the PPF when exchanging with French taxable persons. VAT periodic returns and recapitulative statements are filed electronically via the DGFiP EDI or EPF platforms. Exports require separate export declarations in the Delta G / EXS system of French Customs.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 262 of the French General Tax Code (CGI), supplies of goods dispatched or transported outside the EU are tax-exempt/zero-rated if the exporter establishes that the goods have left the European Union within one month (standard regime; 90 days for intra-EU dispatches under intra-community exemption). Services, including cross-border subtitle transcription, AI dubbing, and post-production services, may be zero-rated where the place of supply is outside France under the B2B general rule (Article 259-1 CGI) or the B2C rules for services supplied to non-EU customers; the supplier must reasonably demonstrate the customer's status and establishment outside France using valid VAT numbers, contracts, and business correspondence; exports of physical media or deliverable goods additionally require proof of shipment to a non-EU destination
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAU) registered in French Customs e-export system
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank transfer/Payment confirmation evidencing proceeds repatriation
Commercial invoice issued by the French SARL
Packing list and transport contract (CMR, AWB, sea waybill)
VAT number and business registration confirmation of the non-EU customer
Service contract or purchase order for AI subtitle transcription and dubbing services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The French tax administration may retrospectively claw back zero-rated VAT where export or cross-border supply documentation is missing, incomplete, or fraudulent. Under Articles 1728 to 1731 CGI, understated VAT attracts an automatic 40% penalty (or 80% for bad faith or abuse of law), late payment interest of 0.20% per month, and possible discretionary countervailing penalties of up to 10% to 30%. Customs fraud penalties (Article 414 and 423 of the Code des Douanes) include seizure of goods, fines of one to three times the evaded duties/taxes, and imprisonment in case of false export declarations. AI subtitle and dubbing vendors are specifically exposed to cross-border digital services audits; the service provider must retain a complete audit trail of user IP logs, delivery timestamps, payment rails, and consignee evidence for at least 10 years to support zero-rating substantiation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Directorate General for Statistics and Balance of Payments) in coordination with the Direction Générale du Trésor for exchange-control policy, and the ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution) for banking supervision and AML/CFT enforcement. The legal basis is the Code monétaire et financier (Articles L.221-1 to L.224-4 and R.221-1 et seq.) plus EU Treaty Article 63 TFEU on free movement of capital.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France has full euro convertibility. Current-account transactions (cross-border services, royalties, subcontracting fees) and capital movements require no exchange-control authorization, subject to (i) EU/international sanctions, (ii) the French FDI screening regime (IEF, Décret n°2019-1590) for sensitive sectors — not triggered by ISIC 5912 subtitle/AI dubbing — and (iii) mandatory ex-post statistical reporting to Banque de France. Profit remittance: no prior FX approval; a SARL may distribute dividends to non-resident shareholders by bank transfer, but the paying bank applies 25% French withholding tax (30% for non-treaty states) subject to treaty or EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief, and typically requires the shareholder's tax-residence certificate, the gérant's distribution resolution, and audited accounts to evidence distributable reserves. Practical friction: non-EEA shareholders with opaque intermediate structures face extended enhanced due diligence and source-of-wealth review before remittance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender or conversion rule exists in France. The SARL may lawfully retain USD, GBP and other export proceeds in foreign-currency accounts (comptes en devises) at any ACPR-licensed bank without central-bank approval. However, each cross-border cash transaction with a non-resident exceeding EUR 75,000 in a single operation must be declared ex-post via the Banque de France OTRE platform (Opérations de Transactions avec l'Étranger), using the COFERCI purpose-code nomenclature; the bank will file this on behalf of the client when the transfer is executed through it. Factoring and receivables discounting of export invoices are freely permitted.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (Compte Commercial) and segregated Capital Escrow Account via BNP Paribas Corporate & Institutional Banking
Operational Account and FX Hedging Line under a French Master Agreement (AFB/ISDA)
Operational / Escrow hybrid with euro clearing through CRI network
Operational Account for domestic collections and statutory payments
Operational and collection accounts with regional onboarding

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High for operating treasury and payout collection; Medium for capital escrow. ACPR-licensed or registered payment institutions (Wise Platform, Qonto, Revolut Business, Treezor, MangoPay) provide remote onboarding, virtual IBANs, multi-currency accounts and direct integration with Stripe/Wise rails. Legal constraint: EMIs are not credit institutions; funds held are not covered by the FGDR deposit guarantee and cannot be held as a regulated escrow account. Therefore the recommended structure is: EMI for receivables collection and daily disbursements, Tier-1 bank for the capital escrow, FX hedge line and any documentary guarantees.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory obligation for the gérant to appear physically; remote onboarding via video KYC and eIDAS-qualified electronic signature is permitted for EU/EEA directors by ACPR-regulated banks (e.g., BNP Hello Pro, Société Générale Pro remote flow). For a non-EU director, French Tier-1 banks invariably require one physical branch visit or a bank delegation visit; alternatively, appoint a French domiciliation agent (CRC) holding a notarized power of attorney and present apostilled/certified-translated identity documents. EMIs accept fully remote onboarding but impose stricter proof-of-address and source-of-funds checks for non-EU shareholders.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: AI voice-cloning and automated subtitle activity generating 'negative news' or media-sector scrutiny in first-line compliance screening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business plan, existing client contracts evidencing licensed IP and lawful re-use; CNIL GDPR registration and data-protection impact assessment covering cloned-voice consent; model-training provenance records; and confirmation that ISIC 5912 is classified as Low_Risk_Standard under the bank's sector risk matrix.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident, non-EU ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) with a multi-layer intermediate parent structure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Kbis extract (less than 3 months), certified statutes, Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (UBO filing) transcript, full corporate chart of the parent, passport and proof of address of the UBO, reference letter from the UBO's home bank, and source-of-wealth statement for the capital contribution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Shareholder loan / parent-company capital top-up classified as risky inbound credit.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written convention de trésorerie approved by the gérant, board minutes, arm's-length interest-rate justification or explicit interest-free waiver, latest audited accounts of the shareholder, and a cash-flow forecast demonstrating repayment capacity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Marketplace omnibus settlement from Stripe/Wise flagged as third-party pass-through or unidentified counterparty.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Platform settlement statements per payout batch, corresponding client invoices (factures) for subtitle/dubbing work, proof of merchant-of-record status on the platform, and an ISO 20022 remittance reference linking each batch to specific purchase orders.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Substance concerns where the SARL has no French premises and all IP is held abroad.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: French commercial lease or CRC domiciliation contract, local subcontractor or employment agreements, VAT registration (TVA intracommunautaire), transfer-pricing documentation (form n°2257), and an economic-substance memo evidencing French post-production and quality-control activity.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Share-capital and shareholder-loan injection: (a) EUR from EEA — SEPA Credit Transfer via Target2/EBA STEP2 with remittance field 'Apport de capital / avance d'associé – SARL [name] – Kbis [number]'; (b) non-EEA or non-EUR — SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 for interbank credit) to the SARL's IBAN with the Banque de France OCE purpose code for capital operations ('500' series) or commercial services ('200' series); for a capital increase, the bank requires either an inserted notarial deed or a gérant resolution plus legal publication notice; non-cash contributions (IP, license rights) must be supported by a commissaire aux apports valuation report. Expected contributions should be pre-notified to the relationship manager to prevent automatic freezing.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier and subcontractor settlement: (i) intra-EEA EUR invoices — SEPA CT (pain.001) with ISO 20022 purpose code 'TRAD'/'GDDS' and invoice number; (ii) non-EEA USD/GBP — SWIFT MT103 via correspondent banking with CHIPS UID, attaching the FX reference and the Banque de France BOP service code for audiovisual services; initial vendor settlements may use documentary collection (D/P at sight); for high-volume dubbing/subcontracting, a standby or payment LC under UCP600 is permissible but the cost-efficient standard is a fully invoice-matched MT103; all statutory payments (URSSAF, DGFiP, CNIL fees) must remain on domestic SEPA rails.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable EUR/USD FX forward (tenor up to 12–24 months) under ISDA or French AFB Master Agreement — primary hedge for USD revenue settled through Stripe/Wise
FX swap or swap roll-over to align hedging with floating platform payout dates
Cross-currency swap (EUR/USD or EUR/GBP) to match a long-term non-EUR shareholder loan or WB debt
Purchased plain-vanilla EUR/USD and EUR/GBP options for downside protection (premium-payable only; no net short option writing without regulatory capital)

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) permitted solely for restricted or thinly convertible emerging-market currencies (e.g., certain Asian/African local units); NDFs are unnecessary and not offered for EUR/USD as the offshore market is fully deliverable
Interest-rate swaps / EURSTR-based collars on the corporate credit facility to fix lending margins if the Tier-1 bank extends a treasury line

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Court Registry through the INPI formalities portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Approve accounts within six months after financial year-end; file within one month after approval, or two months for electronic filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court injunction and potential daily penalty; manager fine generally EUR 1,500, increasing to EUR 3,000 for repeat offending. France has no automatic annual-return strike-off deadline.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return, Form 2065 and supporting schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally the second business day after 1 May for calendar-year companies; otherwise within three months after financial year-end, subject to the applicable electronic filing calendar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may trigger a 10% surcharge, late-payment interest generally at 0.20% per month, and additional assessments or tax penalties. No separate corporate strike-off is automatically triggered.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial-owner information update, where a change occurred
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Court Registry through the INPI formalities portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: File within 30 days after any change affecting beneficial ownership or related identification information; no routine annual confirmation is required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file may result in formal notice, court-ordered compliance, penalties for the legal representative, and restrictions affecting registry compliance. No automatic annual strike-off timeline applies.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor is generally mandatory when the SARL exceeds at least two of three thresholds: EUR 5 million balance-sheet total, EUR 10 million net annual turnover excluding tax, and 50 average employees. Additional group-company rules may apply.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French Generally Accepted Accounting Principles under the French Accounting Standards Authority (ANC). IFRS is not generally mandatory for standalone SARL accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not require a routine annual UBO confirmation. The company must update the beneficial-owner filing within 30 days after any ownership, control, identity, or address change. Share transfers must be documented and reflected in the shareholder and share-transfer records.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register or record of management decisions
Minutes of shareholder meetings and written shareholder decisions
Accounting books and supporting accounting documentation

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 650-2,200 annually for commercial domiciliation and basic corporate administrative services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 3,000-10,000 annually for a small SARL subject to statutory audit; higher for complex or group entities

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS); reduced 15% rate applies to the first €42,500 of taxable profit for qualifying SMEs with taxable income attributable to an enterprise meeting the SME turnover test (annual turnover below €10 million and at least 75% held by individuals/qualifying entities).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 10% reduced rate on qualifying IP Box income from patents, patented processes and software (including licensing or embedded software in AI dubbing outputs); exemption of French-source results attributable to foreign permanent establishments under territoriality rules; innovation tax credit (CIR) and innovation tax credit for SMEs (CII); reduced rates under the 'jeune entreprise innovante' (JEI) regime if the SARL qualifies as an innovative growth company.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite carryforward, but the annual offset is capped at €1,000,000 plus 50% of the taxable income exceeding €1,000,000; one-year loss carryback is available up to €1,000,000 under the 'carryback' regime (report en arrière).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: French fiscal 'liasse': Form 2065-SD (déclaration de résultats) plus mandatory annex schedules 2058-A through 2058-C; electronic filing is compulsory via the professional portal impots.gouv.fr (EDI or EFI mode).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return plus four quarterly advance instalment payments of corporate income tax; a balancing payment is due when the annual return is filed.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual return must be filed within three months of the end of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year SARL (FY ending 31 December), the filing deadline is 3 May of the following year; non-calendar-year entities must file no later than three months after the closing date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2065-SD, Cadre A – Identification de la société
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company name, legal form (SARL), French SIREN/SIRET number, registered office address, APE/NAF activity code, RCS registration number, and fiscal year opening/closing dates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a French-resident SARL, enter the French tax ID of the head office and the central tax administration. If the SARL is managed by non-resident directors, the entity itself remains a French tax resident and must file as a domestic entity; a non-resident parent/beneficial owner must not be substituted as the filer unless the SARL has ceased to be managed and controlled in France.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2065-SD, Cadre B – Résultats de l'exercice
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting net profit or loss before tax (bénéfice ou perte comptable) as prepared under French GAAP, including revenue from automated subtitle transcription, AI voice cloning licensing, post-production services and any fees invoiced to foreign clients.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The SARL must report worldwide income attributable to its French business under French corporate tax territoriality rules. Foreign-source income derived through a foreign permanent establishment should be excluded to the extent quarantine is available; income attributable to purely French activities must be included without exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of accounting profit with taxable income, including non-deductible expenses, tax depreciation, provisions, deficit reportable (déficit reportable), and transfer pricing adjustments to intercompany contracts with related production or licensing counterparties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: When a cross-border service arrangement exists (e.g., a foreign parent company provides AI algorithms or owns voice-cloning IP), the French SARL must ensure all payments are arm's length and supported by contemporaneous substance documentation. Under-reporting taxable profit through artificially inflated royalty payments to foreign affiliates is a high-risk area.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation and tracking of allowable tax losses, including the annual cap on carryforward absorption: the first €1,000,000 is absorbed fully, and only 50% of the remaining taxable profit can be absorbed beyond that threshold in any given year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The SARL must keep detailed loss schedules to substantiate carried-forward losses on a per-year basis. Do not mix losses incurred by a foreign affiliate with French losses; only losses realised by the French entity are deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2257-SD – Annexe transfer pricing and related-party transactions (if applicable)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Mandatory disclosure of related-party transactions: nature and amounts of transactions with foreign or domestic associates, allocation of profits, royalties, financing, cost-sharing, and management fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A French SARL controlled by a non-resident parent must file this annex even below the formal transfer pricing documentation threshold if it carries out controlled transactions. Enter precise amounts of intercompany royalty, subtitling, dubbing, and AI processing fees.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a 10% increase of the assessed tax if filed late; 40% increase if the return is not filed within 30 days of a formal demand; 80% for concealment or abusive artificial transactions. Late-payment interest accrues at 0.20% per calendar month. Additional fixed penalties of €100 per omitted statement or annex can apply. Directors are jointly liable for interest and penalties if the failure is imputable to their fault.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Domestic withholding tax under Article 119 bis CGI: 25% on dividends distributed by a French company to a non-resident corporate beneficial owner; 30% for distributions to non-resident individuals; 75% for distributions to a beneficial owner resident in a non-cooperative state (Etat non coopératif). Qualifying EU/EEA parent companies holding at least 10% of the SARL for at least two years may benefit from 0% withholding under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced rate under a double taxation agreement, the non-resident shareholder must provide the French paying company with a valid tax residence certificate (Form 5000/5001) issued by the treaty country, evidencing beneficial ownership of the dividends. The certificate must identify the shareholder, the year of income, and the applicable treaty article. Where the reduced rate is to be applied at source, the certificate must be delivered to the French payer before the payment; alternatively, the excess withholding may be reclaimed through the French tax authorities' refund procedure using Form 5000-R and the relevant treaty relief application. For EU parent companies, Form 5000 plus a statement of direct/indirect holding and holding period is sufficient to apply the 0% parent-subsidiary withholding at source.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties (IP licences, patents, software, AI voice models, subtitling technology): French domestic withholding tax of 33⅓% applies to payments made by a French payer to a non-resident for the use of industrial property rights or royalties under Article 182 B CGI; treaty rates normally range from 10% to 15% on beneficial-owner royalties, and the EU Interest & Royalties Directive may exempt royalties paid to qualifying associated EU companies. Interest on loans: payments to non-residents are generally subject to a 25% statutory withholding tax under Article 119 bis for bond, loan or debt-interest income not exempt; however, arm's-length interest paid to an associated EU company may be exempt under the EU Interest & Royalties Directive if the 25% direct holding test and substance conditions are satisfied; most French tax treaties reduce domestic interest withholding to 0%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400 million of annual turnover or gross assets: a French entity exceeding this threshold must prepare a Local File and Master File under Articles L.13 AA and L.13 AB CGI, plus file Form 2257-SD. For entities below the threshold, the SARL must nonetheless maintain contemporaneous arm's-length evidence for all controlled transactions; tax authorities may require simplified transfer pricing documentation within a period of not less than 30 days after request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France applies no standalone Economic Substance Regulations such as those of UAE/OFC jurisdictions, but the French tax authorities invoke the general anti-abuse rule (Article L.64 LPF), the substance-over-form doctrine, and the concept of 'abus de droit' to disregard artificial arrangements lacking commercial rationale and economic substance. Cross-border deployment of AI subtitling, voice cloning, and IP licences requires genuine French operating substance: local personnel, active management decisions, technical development activity, and contracts aligning profit allocation with value creation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately suppressing sales invoices from AI subtitle services, under-reporting foreign platform revenue, forging expense documents, or failing to file the annual corporate tax return for more than 30 days after formal notice.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of 40% of the assessed tax if the omission is deliberate; 80% if the return contains abusive artificial acts or concealment; criminal penalties under Article 1741 CGI include imprisonment of up to five years and a fine of €500,000; interest at 0.20% per month applies until full payment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers may be jointly and severally liable for the tax, penalties, and interest; in addition, the criminal offence of tax fraud can result in a personal ban on commercial activity, suspension of professional licences, travel bans, and extradition procedures where the director is resident abroad.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Interposing the French SARL as an empty mailbox company with no actual employees, no board decision-making, no premises or activity, while routing subtitling and voice-cloning profits to low-tax foreign entities over which no real operational control or economic substance exists.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Abuse of law (abus de droit) sanction: 80% of the tax reassessment plus late-payment interest; the full amount of the artificial transaction is disregarded and profits are reclassified to the French entity; the tax authorities may also impose into force the 100% penalty under Article 1729 CGI where the abuse has a fraudulent objective.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The managing director (gérant) may face unlimited civil liability if the corporate veil is pierced, and criminal liability under L.64 and Article 1741 where the artificial scheme is proven to be orchestrated with intent; travel bans and seizure of personal assets may follow.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging excessive intercompany royalties, management fees, or service charges to the French SARL for AI software, voice libraries, or subtitling algorithms, without evidence of benefit, actual functionality, personnel, or risk assumption, thereby shifting French taxable profits abroad.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment at the taxpayer's transaction value plus transfer pricing adjustments; 40% penalty in the absence of documentation or if the profit shift is deliberate; interest at 0.20% per month; potential withholding tax recapture on the re-characterised payments under Article 119 bis and Article 182 B.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve or implement non-arm's-length transfer prices may be held jointly liable for the resulting corporate tax and penalties under French criminal law where intent is shown; in severe cases, high-value transfers may be treated as tax evasion and expose directors to fines and imprisonment, together with restrictions on leaving the jurisdiction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Non-Declaration of Foreign Bank Accounts or Payment Rails
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using foreign payment processors (Stripe, Wise) without reporting the necessary foreign accounts pursuant to Article 1649 A CGI, or failing to declare a U.S.-domiciled Stripe/Wise account balance when the threshold and conditions for declaration apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fixed annual fine of €1,500 per account; €150 per unreported transaction if a return is filed but omits a transaction; for accounts located in non-cooperative states, the fine increases to €10,000 per account; full reassessment of unreported income and 40% penalty for failure to file.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative and the beneficial owners have a personal obligation to ensure declarations are made; non-compliance may lead to criminal conviction for concealment of assets, with fines and imprisonment under Article 1741, and travel bans pending investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Making dividend distributions to shareholders, or recording partner withdrawals as 'expenses', without passing the proper shareholder resolution, without recording them in the annual tax return, and without applying the mandatory withholding tax for non-resident shareholders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disallowance of the distribution as a deductible item, reclassification as dividend or salary subject to social liabilities, withholding tax assessed at 25%/30% plus late payment interest and 10% non-filing penalty; refusal of treaty relief where no certified TRC exists.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant is exposed to civil liability toward the company and third parties for distributions not reflecting true corporate profit, and criminal liability for misuse of company assets (abus de biens sociaux) under Articles L.241-3 of the French Commercial Code, carrying up to five years' imprisonment and a €75,000 fine.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating in the film post-production segment with frequent foreign counterparties, collecting payments via Stripe/Wise, and neither identifying the beneficial owners of international clients nor maintaining routine KYC files, thereby facilitating money being laundered through the SIRL revenue stream.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The SARL is not a regulated financial institution for AML purposes, but if it intentionally facilitates tax evasion or money laundering by accepting unreported offshore funds, it faces confiscation of proceeds, criminal fines of up to €375,000 for corporate offenders, and regulatory penalties for misuse of professional activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be criminally charged for complicity in money laundering if they knowingly receive or transfer funds of unlawful origin; penalties include imprisonment of up to five years, fines, travel bans, and commercial activity prohibitions.
